newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar ranged on poor demand, low offerings.
newsitem.headline: India sugar ranged on poor demand, low offerings.

text.p: Sugar prices remained steady in a narrow range on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
Consumer demand was sluggish at the end of the month but scattered supplies kept offerings at a low ebb.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 remained steady at 1,471/1,495 rupees per quintal, as was sugar M-30 at 1,490/1,535 rupees per quintal.
Inflow of sugar from mills to the market remained low as local millers have already sold their allotted quantity of sugar of the free sale quota for July.
"Sugar mill delivery remained unquoted for the same reason," one broker said.
The free sale quota for July is 750,000 tonnes against 800,000 tonnes released in June. The August quota is 750,000 tonnes.
"I am expecting sugar prices to remain firm next month on festival buying," a broker added.
